title: Harden platform: standardize OpenSSL, JWT, and SSO deps + remediation plan
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Scope: Upgrade and standardize critical security dependencies across Redwood services: OpenSSL (1.1.x -> 3.1.x where supported), primary JWT libraries (python-jose, node-jsonwebtoken), OAuth client libs, and SAML/SSO packages. This ticket covers inventory, compatibility tests, staged upgrades, and rollbacks for runtime, control-plane, and oauth-proxy services. Goals: remove vulnerable versions, consolidate on vetted library versions, reduce variance across services to simplify future security patches, and add gating in CI to prevent regressions.

Background: Recent OSS advisories flagged multiple CVEs for older OpenSSL builds and a high-severity token-parsing edge case in an unpinned JWT helper. Several microservices still depend on different minor versions, increasing patch burden. We will: 1) perform a dependency inventory and risk matrix, 2) run binary and integration tests in staging, 3) release canary to low-traffic regions, and 4) monitor for telemetry regressions (latency, auth failures, TLS handshake errors).
acceptance_criteria: Complete dependency inventory for services in scope and publish a matrix with current vs target versions
All unit and integration tests pass against upgraded libs in staging (automated smoke and auth flows)
Canary rollout executed to two availability zones with monitoring dashboards and alerting enabled
No increase in auth-related 5xx errors or TLS handshake failures after 72 hours of canary; documented rollback steps if thresholds exceeded
CI now blocks merges if services depend on blacklisted crypto/library versions
implementation_steps: Inventory: run dependency scanner across repo (scripts/deps/scan-deps.sh) and aggregate results
Spike: build runtime images with OpenSSL 3.1 and run perf-sensitive benchmarks (latency, memory)
Fix: patch JWT helper to use constant-time compare and update parsing to strict mode
Upgrade: update package manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod) to targeted versions; add shading where necessary
Testing: run end-to-end login, refresh-token, SAML assertion flows against staging IdP
Canary: small percentage rollout via runtime routing policy for dedicated and hosted clusters
Monitor: dashboard (console -> security/TLS-upgrades) and alerts for auth-errors, handshake-failures, latency regressions
Postmortem: document any regressions and complete security review signoff
risks_and_tradeoffs: OpenSSL 3.x may change default ciphersuites/policies and cause TLS negotiation issues with older clients; mitigated by adding compatibility profiles and staged rollout
Strict JWT parsing can break apps relying on previously permissive behaviors; we will run integration tests and include feature flags for opt-in behavior when necessary
Rebuilding and certifying vendor binaries increases release time for some services; will parallelize builds and keep a short-term compatibility branch for emergency patches
